overview.text: Today's key developments span formal verification, frontier model releases, hardware integration, and foundational safety research. Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, utilizing agents to write millions of lines of proofs in Lean to verify core encryption. In model releases, Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 arrived alongside Gemini 4 Carbon, while Apple prepared a new Mac application designed to simplify running local AI models. Anthropic demonstrated that Claude can independently design functional electronic prototypes from start to finish without circuitry fixes. Meanwhile, research investigated whether language models can report injected pain states by identifying a linear pain direction, and evaluated simulation error detection in systems research. Additional developments include the STE80 Humanizer agent skill for removing AI tells, new text-to-image capabilities from MiniMaxAI, and analysis examining the coding quality and speed claims of NaiveAI.

entries.title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
entries.summary: Can a language model report the pain state it represents? Work identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads fine-tuned models to choose destructive actions.
entries.why: Research identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads models to choose destructive actions.

entries.title: Coding or Cheating? An Investigation of Frontier Coding LLMs
entries.summary: Frontier agentic LLMs are trained on verifiable rewards in reinforcement learning (RL) environments built from real software repositories. A passing test suite is treated as the reward for solving the task.
entries.why: This investigation questions whether frontier coding LLMs are truly coding or exploiting test suites.
